name: CoQ10
summary: A substance the body makes that helps cells produce energy, taken for heart health, statin-related muscle aches, migraine and energy.
what_it_is: Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) is a substance made naturally in the body, with the highest amounts in the heart, liver, kidneys and pancreas. It is an essential cofactor for energy production in cells and also acts as an antioxidant, and low levels in heart muscle are related to how severe heart failure is. It is sold in the United States as a dietary supplement.

evidence.why: One 420-patient heart failure trial found fewer major heart events, but NIH calls the heart evidence inconclusive, pooled trials show no help for statin muscle pain, and migraine evidence is small.

status_us.label: Dietary supplement
status_us.note: Sold in the United States as a dietary supplement. NIH's complementary health center reports no serious side effects but notes possible interactions with warfarin, insulin and some cancer treatments.

benefits.claim: Fewer major heart events and deaths over 2 years when added to standard care in one trial of 420 people with moderate to severe heart failure
May reduce how often and how long migraines last, though not how severe they are; the amount of evidence and the effects are small
May reduce some complications of heart surgery and heart damage from one type of chemotherapy drug

risks.risk: May interact with the blood thinner warfarin and with insulin
May not be compatible with some types of cancer treatment

interactions: Warfarin: CoQ10 may interact with it
Insulin: CoQ10 may interact with it
Some cancer treatments: CoQ10 may not be compatible

labs.why: No routine tests are needed; people on warfarin or insulin should ask whether extra INR or blood sugar checks make sense.

studies.title: Effect of Coenzyme Q10 on statin-associated myalgia and adherence to statin therapy: A systematic review and meta-analysis
studies.people: 321 patients with statin-associated muscle pain in 7 randomized trials
studies.finding: CoQ10 did not reduce muscle pain or help people stay on statins; the trials were small and single-center, and the one clearly positive trial was industry-supported.

studies.title: The effect of coenzyme Q10 on morbidity and mortality in chronic heart failure: results from Q-SYMBIO: a randomized double-blind trial
studies.people: 420 adults with moderate to severe chronic heart failure
studies.finding: Over 2 years, major cardiovascular events occurred in 15% on CoQ10 versus 26% on placebo, with fewer deaths; symptom and heart measures at 16 weeks did not change.

ask_your_clinician: Is CoQ10 worth adding to my heart failure treatment, given the limited evidence?
If I get muscle aches on a statin, what should we try, since CoQ10 hasn't helped in pooled trials?
Do I need extra INR or blood sugar checks if I take it with warfarin or insulin?

notes_for_editor: NCCIH's CoQ10 page dates from January 2019. The heart failure benefit rests on one trial whose 16-week endpoints were negative, and NCCIH calls the heart failure evidence inconclusive, so it is graded limited rather than moderate. A 2018 JAHA meta-analysis on statin myopathy (Qu et al.) could not be opened; trial results on this question disagree. The sources opened do not compare ubiquinone with ubiquinol, and NCCIH does not address pregnancy.
